answer: Resist sybils with time-bound proof of service, not stake. A new identity begins as a faint ember at near-zero weight, unlocking rewards only after a long unbroken streak of verified microtasks; its weight hardens like sediment into basalt and one failure decays it. Microtasks cross-route over a randomized trellis mesh, so no cluster serves itself, and colluders leak correlated loops that forfeit hardened weight once linked. An attacker must sustain N identities over a long window, cost scaling with N times time, while one cross-check sinks them all.
